transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I… I guess what brings me in is I keep thinking my wife and the kids might be better off if I just didn’t wake up. I’ve been saying I don’t need to see another winter.
Have you been thinking about how you would do it if you were to end your life?
I… I don’t know. Mostly I just think they’d be better off if I didn’t wake up. I’ve said I don’t need to see another winter. That’s as far as I can say.
How long have you been having these thoughts about not waking up?
Since my bowling partner died… about a year and a month ago, I guess. It’s been around since then.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the time since your bowling partner died?
I… I don’t know. Sad, empty… maybe. I haven’t really put a name to it.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like?
Not really. I used to look forward to things… bridge, my garden, helping with the church cooking, even Cubs games. Now I mostly just sit in my chair. Can’t seem to make myself care.
Have you lost or gained a significant amount of weight recently?
I’m not really sure. I don’t keep much track of it… my clothes seem about the same, I think.
Do you feel guilty about anything?

Yes… I suppose I do. I keep thinking about things I did wrong— with him, with my family. Little things, mostly, but they don’t feel little. I just… feel like I’m no good to anybody. Like I’ve got something coming to me.
Do you feel like you're moving more slowly than you used to or having trouble sitting still?
Yes… slower, I guess. My wife says I move like I’m walking through deep snow. Even getting dressed or just crossing the kitchen takes me so long, I… sometimes I just give up before I’ve done much.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy doing?
Not really. I used to like bridge… working in the garden, helping with the church cooking, going to Cubs games. Now I mostly just sit in my chair. I can’t seem to make myself care about any of it.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that others couldn't?
Sometimes… in the evenings. I hear his voice, like it’s coming from the hall or the spare room. My wife says it’s quiet, but I hear him saying I should’ve been there… that I failed him.
How long have you been feeling this way, with no enjoyment in activities and thoughts about not waking up?
Since… since my bowling partner died. That was about a year and a month ago now. It’s been that long, I guess.
Do you find yourself fidgeting or having an inability to sit still?
No… not fidgeting, really. It’s more the opposite. My wife says I move like I’m walking through deep snow. Getting dressed, crossing the kitchen… it takes me so long I sometimes just give up.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by moving like you're walking through deep snow?

It’s just… everything feels slowed down. My wife says I move like I’m walking through deep snow. Getting dressed can take so long I stop halfway, or crossing the kitchen feels like too much. I end up giving up before I’ve done much of anything.
Have you been having any other unusual experiences, like seeing things that aren't there, besides hearing your bowling partner's voice?
No… I don’t think I see things. It’s mostly his voice. Some evenings I hear it clear from the hallway, or that spare room… saying I should’ve been there, that I failed him. My wife says it’s quiet.
Have you ever seen things that aren't there, like shadows or movements, when you're alone or in a quiet space?

No… I don’t really see shadows or anything like that. It’s more… I hear him sometimes, plain as day, from the hallway or the spare room. Saying I should’ve been there. That I failed him. My wife says the house is quiet.
Do you feel like you're restless or have an inability to sit still?

No… not restless, really. It’s more the opposite. I move so slow my wife says it’s like I’m walking through deep snow. Even getting dressed or just going across the kitchen can take me so long I just… stop and give up.
Do you think your slow movement is because you don't want to do things or because your body feels heavy and it's an effort to move?

It feels more like my body’s heavy. I don’t know… I’m not trying to be difficult. My wife says I move like I’m walking through deep snow. Getting dressed, or just crossing the kitchen, can take so long I just stop before I’ve done much.
Do you feel like you're fidgeting or restless when you're sitting or lying down?

No… I’m not fidgeting. It’s more that I can barely get myself moving. My wife says I move like I’m walking through deep snow. Even getting dressed or crossing the kitchen takes so long I just… give up.
How many months have you been feeling this way, with no enjoyment in activities and thoughts about not waking up?
About… thirteen months, I guess. Since my bowling partner died. A year and a month ago.
Do you think your feelings of sadness and not wanting to wake up have been getting worse over the past few months?
Yes… I think so. Lately I keep thinking my wife and the kids might be better off if I just didn’t wake up. I’ve even said… I don’t need to see another winter.
